title: Rousing and assisting grace among the Reformed
source_text: XIX. Distinctio gratiae in excitantem atque adjuvantem, non ita frequens est in Schola Reformata, ut in Schola Romana. Ejus tamen meminit, eamque probare videtur in citata modo homilia doctissimus ille Ferrius. Et ea quoque utuntur in Synodo Dordracena Theologi Britanni.
pass_a_gloss: XIX. The distinction of grace into rousing and assisting, is not so frequent in the Reformed School, as in the Roman School. Yet that most learned Ferry makes mention of it, and seems to approve it in the homily just cited. And the British Theologians also use it in the Synod of Dort.
pass_b_english: Thesis XIX. The distinction of grace into rousing and assisting grace is less common in the Reformed school than in the Roman. Still, the very learned Ferry mentions it in the homily just cited and seems to approve it.
The British theologians at the Synod of Dort use it as well.

lemmas.latin: non ita frequens est in Schola Reformata
lemmas.gloss: is not so frequent in the Reformed School
the British Theologians in the Synod of Dort

choices.why: Kept as in the Roman locus for gratia excitans and adjuvans.

bible_refs: Paul Ferry (1591-1669), pastor at Metz, homily on Hebrews 12:28 (published separately).
Judgement of the British delegation at the Synod of Dort (1618-1619).
